7,693 likes, 373 comments - anahitadhondy on May 7, 2024: "Hi I’m Anahita, thank you for being here 🥹 I don’t think I’ve ever summed it up like this but let’s try ❤️

🐣I Started baking at the age of 10. I’m Parsi, born and raised in Delhi 
🤰My mom’s been a home cook and caterer since I was born she still makes cakes and Parsi food & Parsi masalas and supplies it to restaurants. 
That’s where I learnt how to cook 🫶
👩‍🏫Went to @weareihmaura and studied culinary arts for 3 years while interning every summer vacation at different hotels - Marriott, Taj etc
🏨Worked a full year at @tajmahalhotelnewdelhi in every kitchen dept and then went for my Grande Diplome to @lecordonbleulondon 
🇬🇧Looked for jobs in London but couldn’t get one because of my visa 
👩‍💻Joined The olive group before they were about to open @sbowindia 
Started SBOW In 2013 and expanded the chain till 2021. 
👩‍🍳Alongside in those 9 years, posted pretty frequently on social media and shared a lot of behind the scenes from the kitchen (not sure how many of you followed me then) and worked on the promotion of Millets in the restaurant and on SM. 
💍Married to @arush_bhandari ❤️🧿
🌾Was a part of the @chefsmanifesto and then travelled to a few countries and events to showcase regional Indian food and millets. 
✍️started my own company where I provide F&B solutions, menu consultation, recipe development for brands, social media related work and solutions. 
📕Wrote a cookbook which took 5 years to complete and came out in 2021 - it’s called ‘The Parsi Kitchen’ available in all bookstores and online published by @harpercollinsin 
☺️I don’t know if I’ve missed anything but I’m grateful for every single opportunity. I’ve had ups and downs. 
📈Lows and highs, body cramps and crazy days but I’ve enjoyed what I do every single day and I’ve grateful for all that it gives me. 
🐶 @yuzu_theincredible is our baby puppy and my lifeline! 
🥰I do continue to work in this space - write more books, share more recipes and ultimately whenever in the future open up My own little cafe and bakery in the hills which would also be some kind of culinary school (i love teaching) 🤞🏡

Continued in the caption ..
Do say hi and tell me what do you do / or anything about you 👋🥹".

183 likes, 12 comments - anahitadhondy on October 9, 2026: "The ONE COFFEE CAKE recipe you need ☕🍰 | #AnahitaCooks 👩‍🍳 

A soft, buttery coffee loaf infused with espresso and topped with a smooth coffee glaze. Perfectly balanced between rich coffee flavour and sweetness, this is the ideal bake to pair with your afternoon coffee!

INGREDIENTS
All-purpose flour – 180 g
Cornstarch – 30 g
Baking powder – 2 tsp
Salt – 1/2 tsp
Butter – 100 g, softened
Neutral oil – 2 tbsp
Granulated sugar – 150 g
Eggs – 3 large
Plain yogurt – 120 g
Vanilla extract – 2 tsp
Instant espresso powder or instant coffee – 2 tbsp
Hot water – 2 tbsp
Milk – 50 ml

For the Coffee Glaze
Powdered sugar – 200 g
Brewed espresso or strong coffee – 2–3 tsp

METHOD
1. Preheat the oven to 170°C. Grease and line a 9 × 5-inch loaf tin.
2. ⁠Dissolve the instant coffee in hot water and let it cool slightly.
3. ⁠In a bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and salt.
4. ⁠In another bowl, beat the butter, oil, and sugar until light and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
5. ⁠Mix in the vanilla, yogurt, cooled coffee mixture, and milk.
6. ⁠Gently fold in the dry ingredients until just combined, being careful not to overmix.
7. ⁠Pour the batter into the prepared loaf tin and bake for 50–60 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out with a few moist crumbs.
8. ⁠Allow the cake to cool completely.
9. ⁠For the glaze, whisk the powdered sugar with the brewed coffee until smooth. Drizzle over the cooled cake and let it set before slicing.

#coffeecake #espresso #espressoloaf #teacake".

584 likes, 38 comments - anahitadhondy on October 8, 2026: "THE MODERN HOST - EPISODE 3 ✨

Make it Festive: Corn & Cheese Parcels

Crispy, flaky and filled with the creamiest cheese and corn filling, these little parcels are exactly what you want on a festive table. They’re ridiculously easy to put together, can be prepped ahead, and are perfect for passing around while everyone’s busy chatting, eating and celebrating. Serve them warm with your favourite dip and watch them disappear!

Ingredients

* ½ cup cream cheese
* ¾ cup sweet corn, boiled
* 2 tbsp spring onion, finely chopped
* ½ tsp chilli flakes
* ½ tsp dried oregano
* Salt, to taste
* ½ tsp black pepper
* 1 sheet puff pastry
* Oil, for spraying

Method

1. In a bowl, add cream cheese, sweet corn, spring onion, chilli flakes, oregano, salt and pepper. Mix well.
2. Cut the puff pastry into squares and place a spoonful of the filling in the centre.
3. Fold and seal the pastry into neat little parcels.
4. Lightly spray with oil.
5. Cook in a preheated oven or air fryer at 180°C for 10–15 minutes, or until golden and crisp.
6. Serve warm with your favourite dip.

#AnahitaCooks

171 likes, 18 comments - anahitadhondy on October 7, 2026: "Episode 7/10 of 10 states, 10 rice dishes-  Vagharela Bhaat from Gujarat

Vagharela Bhaat is a comforting Gujarati rice dish that turns simple, everyday ingredients into something incredibly flavourful. The magic is in the vaghar - a fragrant tempering of mustard seeds, jeera, hing, chillies and curry leaves, tossed through leftover rice with onions, ginger and garlic. It’s quick, homely and the perfect way to give yesterday’s rice a delicious second life.

Ingredients
* 2 tbsp oil
* 1 tsp mustard seeds
* 1 tsp jeera
* ¼ tsp hing
* 2–3 dried red chillies
* 8–10 curry leaves
* 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste
* 2 green chillies, finely chopped
* 1 medium onion, finely chopped
* ½ tsp haldi
* 3 cups leftover cooked rice
* Salt, to taste
* 2 tbsp fresh coriander, chopped

Method
1. Heat the oil in a pan and add the mustard seeds. Let them crackle.
2. Add jeera, hing, dried red chillies and curry leaves. Let the tempering sizzle.
3. Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chillies and sauté until fragrant.
4. Add the onions and cook until soft and lightly golden.
5. Add haldi and salt and mix well.
6. Add the leftover cooked rice and gently toss until the tempering coats every grain.
7. Cook for 2–3 minutes until heated through.
8. Finish with plenty of fresh coriander and serve hot.

#AnahitaCooks

403 likes, 27 comments - anahitadhondy on October 5, 2026: "KALA CHANNA CHUTNEY 🌿🌶️ | #AnahitaCooks 👩‍🍳

A delicious, protein-packed chutney made with kala channa, fresh coriander, ginger, garlic, and green chilli. Slightly sweetened with jaggery, it’s a wholesome twist on a classic chutney!

INGREDIENTS

Oil – 1 tsp (used mustard oil) 
Green chilli – 1
Garlic – 2 cloves
Ginger – 1-inch piece
Cooked kala channa – 1/2 cup

Fresh coriander – 1/2 cup
Salt – to taste
Jaggery – 1 tsp
Water – as needed
Lemon juice or amchoor as needed to sour it. 

METHOD

1. Heat oil in a pan and add the green chilli, garlic, and ginger. Sauté until fragrant.
2. ⁠Add the cooked kala channa and cook for a few minutes until everything is well combined.
3. ⁠Transfer the mixture to a blender. Add fresh coriander, salt, jaggery, and a little water.
4. ⁠Blend until smooth, adding more water as needed to reach your desired consistency. Add lemon and mix. 
5. ⁠Serve fresh as a dip or chutney. 🌿✨

#chutney #condiment #easyrecipe #indian".
